ledger.note: 1567: Hesse-Darmstadt is formed. 'It was formed in 1567 following the division of the Landgraviate of Hesse among the four sons of Landgrave Philip I'; George I received the former upper County of Katzenelnbogen.

region.text: the upper County of Katzenelnbogen round Darmstadt

ledger.note: 1604: Louis IV of Marburg dies and Darmstadt takes Giessen. 'After Louis IV's death in 1604, the dispute continued until the eve of the 1648 Peace of Westphalia'; Louis V 'founded the Lutheran University of Giessen in 1607'.

region.text: Giessen and Biedenkopf, from the Marburg inheritance

ledger.note: 1627: Kassel cedes land to Darmstadt. 'After being forced to cede some of his territories to Hesse-Darmstadt, Maurice abdicated in 1627' (Hesse-Kassel page); the land is the Marburg area, the researcher's reading.

1648: Marburg goes to the elder Kassel line. 'The conflict was finally settled on the eve of the 1648 Peace of Westphalia. Large parts of the disputed Upper Hesse territory, including Marburg, fell to the elder Kassel line. Hesse-Darmstadt retained Giessen and Biedenkopf.'

1736: Hanau-Lichtenberg falls to Darmstadt. 'With count Johann Reinhard III the last male member of the Hanau family died in 1736'; the county 'fell to the Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt because Countess Charlotte' married the future Louis VIII; its centre lay in lower Alsace (Buchsweiler) under French sovereignty since 1680.

ledger.note: 1803: the Final Recess enriches Hesse-Darmstadt. 'Most notable was the acquisition of the Duchy of Westphalia', held by the Prince-Archbishop of Cologne (mediatisation page: 'Cologne: Duchy of Westphalia' and 'Worms: right bank' go to Hesse-Darmstadt).

region.text: the Duchy of Westphalia round Arnsberg

ledger.note: 1803: territories of Mainz and Worms. Hesse-Darmstadt 'received lands from the Prince-Archbishop of Mainz and the Prince-Bishop of Worms'; the page names no places, so the right-bank Rhine area round Heppenheim is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 1803: Hanau-Lichtenberg is divided. 'In 1803 ... Everything left of the Rhine went to France, and everything right of the river went to the Grand Duchy of Baden' (the county page's wording; Baden was then an electorate).
1806: Hesse-Darmstadt becomes a grand duchy. 'Louis X joined the Napoleonic Confederation of the Rhine and took the title of Grand Duke of Hesse.'

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (4 pages opened for this dossier; the Hanau-Lichtenberg page is new here). New state: Cliopatria's 'Grand Duchy of Hesse' starts only in 1806.

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS: Darmstadt 30 km, Giessen 30 km, Biedenkopf (8.53E 50.91N) 15 km, Marburg 30 km, Buchsweiler/Bouxwiller (7.48E 48.82N) 25 km, Arnsberg (8.06E 51.40N) 40 km for the Duchy of Westphalia, Heppenheim (8.65E 49.64N) 25 km for the Mainz and Worms lands. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Darmstadt', 'Biedenkopf', 'Arnsberg', 'Heppenheim', 'Buchsweiler' (Bouxwiller), 'Duchy of Westphalia' (region).

NOT SETTLED. (1) Hanau-Lichtenberg (the Hessian Alsace) was under French sovereignty from 1680; whether it should be drawn as Darmstadt land, a French vassal or neither is open. (2) The 1622 Homburg and 1627 Rotenburg secessions are on the page without saying from which house; not recorded. (3) The 1803 gain from Mainz and Worms has no named places on the page. (4) The Westphalia hand-over is placed in 1803 by the page; the year of the Duchy's transfer to Hesse-Darmstadt within 1803 is not stated. (5) Rheinhessen and the Worms right bank are not on the Darmstadt page (the mediatisation page gives 'Worms: right bank'). (6) 1704-1713 and the French occupations of the Rhineland are not on the pages opened.
